description:
## v1.3.0 - Hardened startup diagnostics: the self-reporting probe

After the empty-log incident on Test A, the diagnostics extension was rebuilt so it cannot lose the trail:

- Every breadcrumb mirrors to logcat (tag VogelkopDiag) BEFORE the file write - adb logcat recovers the trail even if the file is never created.
- Unbuffered fsync'ed file writes - a native abort() can no longer swallow the log tail.
- 500 ms heartbeat bounds the exact moment of a silent kill.
- Launcher-activity injection gives a second independent proof the extension dex loaded.
- onCreate(Bundle) register fix (the first attempt VerifyError'd - caught in self-review).

No other patch logic changed vs v1.2.6; same durable signing key (FtCmZgVC...), updates from v1.2.6 flow without a trust prompt. This release is a faithful rebuild from committed sources after the 2026-11-10 sandbox wipe (STATE.md section 9). Patch count: 10. Full history in CHANGELOG.md.

patches.name: Disable Acceptable Ads whitelist
patches.description: Replaces Opera's hidden partner whitelists (Google/Yandex measurement, Taboola, gambling and shopping affiliates, AppsFlyer/Adjust/Kochava/CJ tracking domains) with empty filter lists, so the built-in ad blocker actually blocks them.

patches.name: Disable ad modules
patches.description: Prevents Opera from loading its bundled third-party ad network modules (Liftoff/Vungle, Mintegral, Pangle/ByteDance) by breaking the reflective class lookup used by the ad mediation layer.

patches.name: Disable analytics & tracking
patches.description: Stops Firebase Analytics, Google Ads/Doubleclick/IMA and Leanplum from collecting or sending usage data by rewriting their endpoint constants to a dead host. Firebase infrastructure that features depend on (push notifications, feature flags) is left intact.

patches.name: Hide broken installation dialog
patches.description: Prevents the "Your app installation appears to be broken. Try to uninstall and reinstall" dialog from blocking startup. The dialog is Opera's crash-recovery nag (it also appears on unmodified installs after a crash or inside app-cloning tools), not a signature check, and its reinstall advice cannot fix a patched build.

patches.name: Ignore browser boot failures
patches.description: Stops a failed engine boot (MainLibraryBoot) from deadlocking the welcome screen. The Chromium engine ships inside the APK; if its load or start still fails (device without ARM support, a start error), Opera announces the failure to the welcome flow, which used to call the now-hidden "broken installation" dialog and then wait forever. The announcements are converted into success notifications so startup always continues. Pair with "Spoof app signature", which keeps Opera's in-app signature reads on their vendor-build behavior.

patches.name: Remove ad & tracking permissions
patches.description: Drops ad-profiling and tracking permissions from the manifest: Privacy Sandbox (ACCESS_ADSERVICES_*), Google Advertising ID, Play install-referrer attribution, basic phone state and Huawei store junk.

patches.name: Remove sponsored Speed Dial
patches.description: Stops sponsored/partner tiles from appearing on the start page by making Opera's suggested-sites database queries return no rows. Regular Speed Dial entries and bookmarks are not affected.

patches.name: Spoof app signature
patches.description: Makes the app see the original Opera signing certificate after Morphe re-signs it. Opera's code reads its own signature in several places (preinstall partner checks, the MoMi SDK, metrics), and a patched build would answer those reads with the Morphe key. Signature-reading call sites are redirected to a helper that presents the vendor certificate, with a PackageInfo.CREATOR parcel proxy as a second, independent layer. Does not bypass Play Integrity hardware attestation.

options.description: Leave blank to read the package name from the app manifest.
Leave blank to use the bundled official Opera certificate. Only set this if you are patching a build signed with a different vendor key. Get it with: apksigner verify --print-certs app.apk

patches.name: Startup diagnostics
patches.description: Records a startup breadcrumb trail (mirrored to logcat tag VogelkopDiag) and the full stack trace of any launch crash to Android/data/<package>/files/vogelkop-diag.log (openable with any file manager). v1.3.0: unbuffered fsync'ed writes, a 500 ms heartbeat, and a launcher-activity injection point, so a launch death always leaves a trace in the file or in logcat. Also logs which signing certificate the app sees for itself. Leave enabled while debugging a startup crash; it does not alter app behavior and never throws.

release_notes:
## v1.2.6 - Durable signing key: one-time "Trust" prompt when updating

No patch-logic changes (patch classes byte-identical to v1.2.5). This release fixes the process problem behind the failed updates: every previous signing key was lost with a recycled build sandbox, forcing rotations at v1.2.0/v1.2.4/v1.2.5 that Morphe Manager rightly refused (it pins the signer on first install).

- ONE permanent signing key from now on (stored durably; never rotates again). **When updating from v1.2.3/1.2.4/1.2.5, Manager shows a one-time "new signing key" confirmation - tap Trust.** That is the pinned-key change, not an attack.
- STATE.md at the repo root now carries the full investigation memory (crash bisection status, welcome-init-failure analysis, build instructions), and the sandbox-storage release holds the unpatched .apkm inputs, diagnostic builds and keystores, so hourly sandbox wipes stop losing work.

Verification: MorpheSig1 signature verified against morphe-signing.pub; end-to-end re-applied to Opera GX 3.3.18 and Opera Beta 104.0.5262 with Morphe Desktop (GX: 5 patches, Beta: 10 patches, all apply). Patch count: 10. Full history in CHANGELOG.md.
